review_candidates.title: Principal Software Engineer (Networking) - Platform Infra
review_candidates.description: Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI. What is The Role: We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to join Platform Infrastructure - Application Networking and set where Elastic Cloud application networking goes next. This work covers Ingress, security controls, private connectivity, and DNS management — the path every interaction with Elasticsearch, Kibana, and the broader Elastic stack takes. You will drive the technical vision, architecture, and design of these systems, not just execute against an existing roadmap. This is a Principal-level role for an engineer who has designed high-performance, scalable networking platforms and can drive technical initiatives across organizations. Elastic is investing in the reliability, security, and reach of Elastic Cloud; you will hold a high bar for those qualities while other engineering teams rely on what this platform provides. What You Will Be Doing: Set the technical direction for major application networking initiatives, owning designs from proposal through general availability. Lead the development of Ingress, private connectivity, DNS, and security controls on a large scale for Elastic Cloud. Continuously identify and address issues related to performance, reliability, and operability. Lead multi-quarter, cross-organizational projects that other Elastic engineering teams rely on, and guide these projects through to delivery. Raise the operational quality of our services. Take charge of operational investigations from beginning to end. Lead complex incident investigations and reviews. Participate in on-call rotation. Mentor and support engineers across the team, serve as a subject matter expert and trusted technical advisor to the wider engineering organization, and set the standard for how we build software. Partner with and advise product management and senior engineering stakeholders on technical trade-offs, feasibility, and roadmap direction. Identify and champion improvements to security, stability, and cost efficiency before they become problems. Untangle complexity and bring architectural clarity across the platform. What You Bring: Experience with building software, including setting technical direction for complex distributed systems running production at scale (Staff or Principal level, or equivalent scope). Deep expertise in application networking and cloud-native architecture. You should understand how services communicate at scale. Knowledge of how to design, operate, and evolve Ingress, private connectivity, DNS, and security controls is required. You have experience building large-scale distributed systems, rather than making use of off-the-shelf services. You are able to own projects from beginning to end. This covers both technical design and working with others to develop needed components. You have experience guiding work involving multiple engineers. You have operated high-availability SaaS platforms, responded to incidents, and improved reliability over time. You care about the quality of work shipped — testing, observability, and operability. You have a proven track record of using AI to accelerate development, debug complex systems, and optimize code, while still owning the final outcomes. You possess the ability to collaborate across functions and teams and seamlessly transition between different projects, codebases, or teams based on business priorities. You can work autonomously, drive decisions and results in a distributed team by leveraging asynchronous, direct, and transparent communication. You communicate clearly and can influence direction across teams and levels without formal authority. Bonus Points: Hands-on experience with Kubernetes networking (Cilium, external-dns, Envoy Gateway, and Crossplane) and with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and its networking ecosystem. You have contributed to CNCF or other open-source networking projects Additional Information - We Take Care of Our People: As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do. We strive to have parity of benefits across regions, and while regulations differ from place to place, we believe taking care of our people is the right thing to do. Competitive pay based on the work you do here and not your previous salary Health coverage for you and your family in many locations Ability to craft your calendar with flexible locations and schedules for many roles Generous number of vacation days each year Increase your impact - We match up to $2000 (or local currency equivalent) for financial donations and service Up to 40 hours each year to use toward volunteer projects you love Embracing parenthood with a minimum of 16 weeks of parental leave Security & Privacy Responsibilities: Take ownership of protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of organizational data and systems by following applicable privacy and security policies, standards, and procedures. Ensure that all individual contributions follow Elastic’s Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF). Proactively participate in mandatory role-based training to ensure personal technical execution consistently aligns with the highest standards of data protection, data privacy, and system resilience. Different people approach problems differently. We need that. Elastic is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating an inclusive culture that celebrates different perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law, ordinance or regulation. We welcome individuals with disabilities and strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all individuals. To request an accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email candidate_accessibility@elastic.co. We will reply to your request within 24 business hours of submission. Applicants have rights under Federal Employment Laws and can view the following posters linked below: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) Poster Employee Polygraph Protection Act (EPPA) Poster Elasticsearch develops and distributes technology and information that is subject to U.S. and other countries’ export controls and licensing requirements for individuals who are located in or are nationals of the following sanctioned countries and regions: Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, or Russia, including the Ukrainian territories annexed by Russia (The Crimea region of Ukraine, The Donetsk People's Republic (DNR), The Luhansk People's Republic (LNR), Kherson or Zaporizhzhia). If you are located in or are a national of one of the listed countries or regions, an export license may be required as a condition of your employment in this role. Please note that national origin and/or nationality do not affect eligibility for employment with Elastic. Please see here for our Privacy Statement. Compensation for this role is in the form of base salary. This role does not have a variable compensation component. At Elastic, our compensation philosophy aims to provide fair, competitive and transparent remuneration. Salary ranges are established based on a combination of external market benchmarks, internal pay equity considerations, and the responsibilities and complexity associated with each role. This approach helps ensure consistency across comparable roles while remaining competitive within the relevant labour markets. The final compensation offered within the applicable range will be determined based on several objective factors, including relevant professional experience, level of skills and expertise, alignment with the role requirements, and the overall scope and complexity of the position. The typical starting salary range for this role is: €73.300—€115.900 EUR

review_candidates.title: Backend Engineer - Platform Core
review_candidates.description: Backend Engineer (Golang) – Platform Core Location: Remote, European time zones, Full-time, Permanent About FullEnrich Every go-to-market motion runs on data, but no single provider has ever had complete coverage. We solve that problem with waterfall enrichment: instead of relying on a single data source, we orchestrate 20+ premium providers around the world, automatically querying them until we find the best available contact information. The result is industry-leading coverage and data quality, helping sales and GTM teams connect with the right people faster. What started as a better way to find emails and phone numbers has grown into a broader vision: becoming the trusted B2B data layer powering modern revenue teams and AI-driven workflows alike. Today, more than 5,000 customers, including companies like AWS, Deel, HubSpot, Clay, and Artisan, trust us to power their prospecting and enrichment. Founded in Paris and now headquartered in San Francisco, we're a team of 50+ people across the US, Europe, LATAM, and Israel, growing quickly and building with speed, ownership, and ambition. That's where you come in. About The Role At the heart of FullEnrich is our waterfall engine. It's the system responsible for deciding which data providers to call, in what order, under which conditions, and what happens when something fails. It works well today, but what we're building next is significantly more ambitious. We're evolving the engine to become far more flexible and configurable, supporting account-specific requirements, dynamic routing based on different optimization goals, and seamless integration of new providers and behaviors without introducing unnecessary complexity. This is a foundational part of our product, and getting the architecture right is critical to how we scale. We're looking for an experienced Backend Engineer who enjoys solving complex infrastructure challenges and taking ownership of the systems behind them. If you've built high-throughput routing systems, designed multi-provider orchestration layers, or worked on infrastructure that needs to adapt to different customers and use cases, this is exactly the kind of challenge you'll be taking on. What You'll Do Own and evolve our core routing engine: Take ownership of provider selection, fallback logic, load balancing, and queue management. Our waterfall currently operates as a modular Go monolith, and you'll help evolve it to support account-level customization at scale without introducing unnecessary complexity. Build and improve provider integrations: Design how we connect to and manage third-party data providers, focusing on rate limiting, reliability, and observability. This includes supporting external provider credentials, configurable provider ordering, and well-defined fallback behavior when providers are unavailable. Develop intelligent routing capabilities: Build the logic that dynamically selects providers based on different optimization objectives, including speed, coverage, compliance, and intelligent load balancing, while managing rate limits effectively. Design scalable multi-tenant architecture: Develop the foundations for sub-accounts, customer-specific credit pools, and endpoint-level configuration, ensuring the engine remains flexible, scalable, and maintainable. Build composable verification workflows: Integrate validity and compliance checks into the enrichment pipeline as configurable steps, allowing results to be independently verified regardless of their original data source. Strengthen our core architecture: Improve and refactor existing systems as we scale, applying strong engineering practices to keep our codebase clean, understandable, reliable, and easy to maintain. Shape technical decisions: Work closely with our engineering leadership to translate product requirements into thoughtful architectural solutions, balancing immediate needs with long-term scalability. What Success Looks Like In your first 3 months: Develop a deep understanding of our existing waterfall engine, provider integrations, and core backend architecture. Build strong relationships with the engineering team and identify opportunities to improve reliability, performance, and maintainability. Start contributing to the evolution of our routing engine, taking ownership of initial architectural improvements and technical decisions. By 6 Months Take ownership of key components of our core platform, delivering meaningful improvements to provider orchestration, fallback logic, and routing capabilities. Help introduce more flexible, account-level configuration while keeping the architecture clean, scalable, and maintainable. Improve the reliability and observability of our provider integrations, reducing operational complexity as we scale. By 12 Months Play a leading role in delivering a more intelligent, configurable waterfall engine that supports different customer needs and optimization goals at scale. Establish robust architectural foundations for multi-tenancy, composable verification, and continued provider expansion. Be a trusted technical contributor within the engineering team, helping shape long-term architectural decisions and ensuring our core platform remains reliable, performant, and ready for future growth. What We're Looking For Strong backend engineering experience: You've built and maintained production systems involving routing, fallback mechanisms, queues, concurrency, and rate limiting. You understand how distributed and multi-provider systems behave under pressure and how to design for reliability. An architecture-first mindset: You're comfortable taking a product requirement, identifying potential structural challenges, and designing solutions that will stand the test of time. You think beyond implementation and consider scalability, maintainability, and long-term impact. Deep experience with Golang: Go is at the core of our backend. You're confident working with modular architectures, clean code principles, and ideally hexagonal architecture. Experience managing technical complexity: You can navigate systems with multiple interconnected components, from account-level configuration and provider orchestration to compliance workflows and multi-tenancy, without compromising clarity or simplicity. Strong ownership and problem-solving skills: You're proactive, pragmatic, and comfortable making technical decisions. You enjoy getting into the details, understanding why systems behave the way they do, and finding solutions to challenging engineering problems. A collaborative approach: You communicate clearly, challenge ideas constructively, and enjoy working with other engineers to build reliable, high-quality systems. Nice to Have Experience with data routing, enrichment pipelines, or multi-provider orchestration systems. Experience building API marketplace infrastructure or multi-tenant SaaS backends. Familiarity with API-first product architectures. An interest in the evolving data infrastructure landscape. Our Tech Stack Our backend is built primarily in Golang , following a modular, hexagonal architecture. Our Wider Stack Includes Backend: Go (Golang) Databases & Search: PostgreSQL, OpenSearch Infrastructure: DigitalOcean, Docker CI/CD: GitHub Actions Monitoring & Observability: Grafana You'll be joining an engineering team of around 10 people, working on one of the most critical components of our platform. Interview Process We aim to keep our process straightforward, transparent, and focused on getting to know each other. Introduction to FullEnrich with our Talent team (30 min) – A chance to learn more about you, introduce FullEnrich and the role, and explore whether there's a mutual fit. CTO & VP Engineering Interview (60 minutes): A conversation about your experience, the role, and a technical discussion based on a real experiment. Technical Assessment: A take-home exercise completed in your own time, followed by a review and discussion. Team & Culture Interview: Meet with a member of the team to learn more about how we work together and ensure there's a strong mutual fit. FullEnrich is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or disability.

You’d be one of its founding engineers, working directly with the Engineering Lead to decide how it’s built. What you’ll do Design and build the core platform and the software around it: integrations, APIs, data flows and tooling. Own how it runs: CI/CD, infrastructure as code, deployment, hosting, scaling and observability. Make the architecture calls, and be able to explain why. Work with energy modellers, analysts and internal developers to turn their problems into platform features. Mentor a small team of a junior engineer and two associates (no line management). Data: Databricks, Postgres, S3, caching and pipelines. UI: lightweight React and TypeScript. AI tooling: GitHub Copilot with all vendors’ models from day one. What we’re looking for A software engineer first. Backend-leaning, writing clean, well-tested code in a high-level language. Someone who builds the framework, not just fits into one. Here’s the test: could you build a platform like Databricks, rather than just use one? Clear communication. You can explain technical trade-offs to non-technical experts. Nice to have: Databricks or Spark, React, and energy or utilities experience. Why this role Impact: your work feeds directly into energy transition and decarbonisation analysis. Greenfield and global: a new platform, a small senior team, and real influence over the architecture. Profit share with a 3-year tail, plus pension, private health, dental and a wellbeing fund. Remote-first: occasional London days, with travel covered if you’re based outside London. A clear process: an intro call, a practical case study (design, discussion and coding in your own environment), then a final conversation with a partner. They are looking for candidates who have built platforms, not just shipped features on them. Paying up to £100k + Bonus scheme + benefits

review_candidates.title: Software Engineer (Native SDKs)
review_candidates.description: 🇪🇬 Up to EUR 20,000 per year, on a full time, contractor contract 🌎 Fully remote working anywhere in Egypt! ✨ High-growth SaaS product trusted by major global sports brands 💻 Modern stack, great tooling, AI-first engineering culture We’re looking for engineers who take initiative, spot opportunities, and move ideas forward proactively. Builders who are excited to use AI as a core part of how they work, think from first principles, and keep things simple – not people who just want to hand-craft every line of code. You’ll be hands-on in our iOS and Android SDKs, primarily in the platform that best matches your experience, working on real features used by major sports and media organisations and using AI heavily to design, build and refine solutions. ABOUT US Storyteller is a high-growth B2B SaaS platform that lets companies integrate Stories into their own apps and websites. Popularised by Instagram and Snapchat, Stories boost engagement, retention and revenue for our clients. Our platform includes SDKs for Web, iOS and Android, publishing tools, analytics and ad support – giving enterprises a complete Stories solution in days. We work with globally recognised sports and media brands, and you’ll see your work used live by millions. About the Role You’ll join the team responsible for our native SDKs, which customers use to embed fast, beautiful, interactive Stories into their iOS and Android apps. Integration quality, performance, backwards compatibility and developer experience really matter. This is a hands-on coding role, but not a “shut the door and code in isolation” one: You’ll use AI tools by default to explore, scaffold and refactor. You’ll think in terms of problems, constraints and outcomes, not just tickets. You’ll care about how easy we are to integrate with as much as how elegant the code looks. You won’t be managing people or owning a team – but you will be expected to own your work end-to-end, contribute to how we solve problems, and help us keep raising the bar. RESPONSIBILITIES Build and ship features Own features end-to-end: understand the problem, design a simple solution, build it (often with AI assistance), test it, and refine based on feedback. Improve performance, reliability, release quality and developer ergonomics across our native SDKs and supporting services. Debug tricky issues across SDKs and customer integrations – using logs, diagnostics and good hypotheses rather than guesswork. Solve real customer problems Work with Product and Delivery to understand real customer use-cases and constraints. Propose simple, pragmatic solutions instead of over-engineering. Help streamline the integration experience so partners can get to “first story live” quickly and safely. Improve developer experience Enhance documentation, code examples, and integration guides, often using AI to draft and then editing for clarity. Identify friction points for integrators and proactively champion improvements. Make small, continuous DX improvements (tooling, scripts, templates) rather than waiting for a big “clean-up project”. Engineering excellence Use AI tools by default for exploration, scaffolding and refactors – and then verify outputs with tests, types, and your own judgement. Use first-principles thinking to cut through complexity: start from the goal and constraints, choose the simplest thing that works, and be willing to delete your own code when a better approach appears. Participate in thoughtful code reviews: give clear, kind, direct feedback and be open to having your own ideas challenged. Help improve CI pipelines, test suites and dev scripts so the whole team moves faster and more safely over time. Maintain high ownership and follow-through from idea to release: surface blockers early, communicate clearly, and finish what you start. QUALIFICATIONS What we’re looking for 2–4 years of hands-on experience building production mobile apps or SDKs in Swift for iOS or Kotlin for Android. Strong knowledge of at least one native mobile platform – iOS with Swift or Android with Kotlin – including its modern frameworks and build tooling. Familiarity with APIs/HTTP , mobile app lifecycles, performance and automated testing. A proactive mindset – you look ahead, anticipate problems, and propose solutions instead of waiting to be told what to do. AI-native working style – you’re comfortable adopting new tools early, especially AI-assisted coding, and you see AI as the default starting point rather than a last resort. Clear reasoning and trade-off thinking – you can explain why you chose one approach over another in simple language. Strong written and verbal communication for remote collaboration. Reliability – you deliver on commitments, surface blockers early, and take responsibility for the quality of your work. You don’t need prior SDK experience or to work across both platforms, but you should be comfortable building libraries and APIs other developers depend on. Nice to have Experience building mobile SDKs, reusable libraries or developer tools. Experience across iOS and Android, or with cross-platform SDKs such as React Native; familiarity with SDK distribution, CI/CD or versioning. Open-source contributions, side projects or technical write-ups that show how you think. Interest in sports, media or content tech. Is this You? This role will likely suit you if: You enjoy figuring out the simplest way to solve a real problem more than endlessly polishing code. You’re happy to lean on AI for a lot of the heavy lifting, and focus your energy on decisions, structure and correctness. You like understanding how your work is used by other developers and care about making their lives easier. It probably isn’t right for you if: Your ideal day is working alone perfecting hand-written code and you’re reluctant to use AI or share ownership. You mainly want to critique AI-generated code or architecture from a distance rather than ship small, concrete improvements regularly. Recruitment Process We keep the process straightforward and respectful of your time. 1. Hiring Manager Conversation (20–30 mins) A short call to get to know you, share more about Storyteller and the Web SDK, and answer your questions. No coding. We’ll both aim to decide whether it makes sense to go deeper. 2. Paid Take-home Task (~60 mins) A small, focused task you can do in your own time. We compensate you for completing it regardless of the outcome. You’re welcome to use AI tools – we’re interested in how you reason, how you verify and simplify, and how you trade off options, not in how much you type. 3. Review and CTO Interview (60–75 mins) We’ll review your submission together, dig into your decisions, and you’ll meet Dave (CTO). We’ll talk about how you approach problems, how you use tools like AI, and how you like to work. And that’s it.
